question: Which of the following is true about "en passant" in chess?

options.text: Only after a pawn moves two squares and waits a turn.
Can be done within two moves after the pawn's advance.
Must be done immediately after the pawn moves two squares.
Only if the capturing pawn is on a dark square.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Must be done immediately after the pawn moves two squares**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **En passant** is a special pawn capture rule in chess that allows a pawn to capture an opponent's pawn immediately after it moves two squares forward from its starting position.
 
• The capture must be made **on the very next move**; otherwise, the opportunity is lost.
 
• The opponent's pawn must have moved two squares forward from its starting position, landing adjacent to the capturing pawn.
 
• When the en passant capture occurs, the capturing pawn moves diagonally to the square where the opponent's pawn would have landed if it had advanced only one square.
 
• The rule was introduced to prevent pawns from bypassing a potential capture when advancing two squares, maintaining fairness in the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pieces & Board**

 
 
• Pieces: King, Queen, Rook, Bishop, Knight, Pawn.
 
• Board: Chessboard, Center (e4, d4, e5, d5), Ranks (rows), Files (columns). 
 
 
 
• **Game States & Results**
 
 
• Check: King is attacked.
 
• Checkmate: King is attacked and cannot escape (Game Over).
 
• Stalemate: No legal moves, but not in check (Draw).
 
• Draw: Tie game (e.g., Perpetual Check, Threefold Repetition).
